title: Isolation Forest
summary: Most anomaly detection methods profile normal instances and then flag deviations, which is costly and can be ineffective when anomalies are few and different. This paper introduces Isolation Forest (iForest), an ensemble of isolation trees that recursively and randomly partitions subsamples; anomalies tend to have shorter average path lengths and receive higher anomaly scores s(x,ψ)=2^{-E(h(x))/c(ψ)}. The authors report that iForest is competitive with or better than ORCA, LOF and Random Forests in AUC while being much faster, especially on large datasets, and that it works even when training contains only normal instances.

requirements.stmt: Build each iTree as a proper binary tree: every internal node has a test of the form q < p and exactly two daughter nodes; every external node has no children and stores the size of the remaining data.
requirements.cite: Section 2, Definition Isolation Tree; Algorithm 2 lines 1-2 and 9-12
requirements.quote: An iTree is a proper binary tree, where each node in the tree has exactly zero or two daughter nodes.

requirements.stmt: Recursively partition a node until e >= l, |X| <= 1, or all data in X have the same values; then return an external node with Size = |X|.
requirements.quote: until either: (i) the tree reaches a height limit, (ii) |X| = 1 or (iii) all data in X have the same values.

requirements.stmt: Set the tree height limit to l = ceiling(log2 ψ).
requirements.quote: l = ceiling(log2 ψ), which is approximately the average tree height

requirements.stmt: For each iTree, draw a subsample X' of size ψ from X by random selection of instances without replacement.
requirements.cite: Section 3 ('sub-sampling is conducted by random selection of instances without replacement'); Algorithm 1 line 4
requirements.quote: Throughout this paper, sub-sampling is conducted by random selection of instances without replacement.

requirements.stmt: At each internal node, randomly select an attribute q uniformly from the list Q of attributes in the current X.
requirements.quote: we recursively divide X by randomly selecting an attribute q and a split value p

requirements.stmt: Select a split point p randomly between the maximum and minimum values of attribute q in the current X.
requirements.quote: randomly select a split point p from max and min values of attribute q in X

requirements.stmt: Partition the data into Xl = filter(X, q < p) and Xr = filter(X, q >= p).
requirements.quote: A test consists of an attribute q and a split value p such that the test q < p divides data points into Tl and Tr.

requirements.stmt: Build an ensemble of t iTrees; the default experiment value is t = 100.
requirements.quote: Unless otherwise specified, we shall use t = 100 as the default value in our experiment.

requirements.stmt: PathLength(x,T,e): if T is external, return e + c(T.size); otherwise compare x_a with T.splitValue, recurse left with e+1 if x_a < splitValue, else recurse right with e+1.
requirements.quote: When x is terminated at an external node, where Size > 1, the return value is e plus an adjustment c(Size).

requirements.stmt: Use c(n) = 2H(n-1) - 2(n-1)/n, where H(i) is the harmonic number and can be estimated by ln(i) + 0.5772156649.
requirements.quote: c(n) = 2H(n −1) −(2(n −1)/n), (1) where H(i) is the harmonic number

requirements.stmt: Compute anomaly score s(x,ψ) = 2^{-E(h(x))/c(ψ)}, where E(h(x)) is the average path length over the forest.
requirements.quote: s(x, n) = 2−E(h(x)) c(n) , (2) where E(h(x)) is the average of h(x) from a collection of isolation trees.

requirements.stmt: Use ψ = 256 as the default sub-sampling size unless otherwise specified.
requirements.quote: Unless otherwise specified, we use ψ = 256 as the default value for our experiment.

requirements.stmt: Compute AUC using anomaly labels only in the evaluation stage; labels must be unavailable during training.
requirements.quote: Anomaly labels are only available in the evaluation stage to compute the performance measure, AUC.

requirements.stmt: Remove all nominal and binary attributes and retain only continuous-valued attributes; for Ionosphere this yields d = 32.
For the high-dimensional irrelevant-attribute experiment only, apply a Kurtosis-based attribute selector per subsample before constructing each iTree.
requirements.quote: We use a simple statistical test, Kurtosis, to select an attribute subspace from the sub-sample before constructing each iTree.

model-based method that explicitly isolates anomalies in-

concept of isolation has not been explored in current liter-
ature. The use of isolation enables the proposed method,

anomalies.

We use eleven natural data sets plus a synthetic data

known anomaly classes as ground truth and these data sets

5.2
Efficiency Analysis
This experiment investigates iForest’s efficiency in re-
lation to the sub-sampling size ψ. Using the two largest
data sets, Http and ForestCover, we examine the effect
of sub-sample size on detection accuracy and processing
time. In this experiment we adjust the sub-sampling size
ψ = 2, 4, 8, 16, ..., 32768.
Our findings are shown in Figure 6. We observe that
AUC converges very quickly at small ψ. AUC is near opti-
mal when ψ = 128 for Http and ψ = 512 for ForestCover,
and they are only a fraction of the original data (0.00045
for Http and 0.0018 for ForestCover). After this ψ setting,
the variation of AUC is minimal: ±0.0014 and ±0.023
respectively. Also note that the processing time increases
very modestly when ψ increases from 4 up to 8192. iFor-
est maintains its near optimal detection performance within
this range. In a nutshell, a small ψ provides high AUC and
low processing time, and a further increase of ψ is not nec-
essary.

"""Isolation Forest, re-implemented from the paper's Algorithm 1-3.

Maps to the claim contract requirements:
  R1  every internal node has one test (q < p) and exactly two daughters;
      every external node has no children and stores Size = |X|.
  R2  recursion stops when e >= l, |X| <= 1 or the node cannot be split.
  R3  height limit l = ceil(log2 psi).
  R4  each tree trains on a sub-sample of size min(psi, n) drawn without
      replacement.
  R5  at each internal node an attribute q is drawn uniformly from the
      attributes present in the current X.
  R6  the split point p is drawn uniformly from [min(q), max(q)).
  R7  X_l = {x : x_q < p}, X_r = {x : x_q >= p}.
  R9  PathLength(x, T, e): e + c(T.size) at an external node, otherwise
      x_q < p ? PathLength(left, e+1) : PathLength(right, e+1).
  R10 c(n) = 2 H(n-1) - 2 (n-1)/n.
  R11 s(x, psi) = 2 ** (-E[h(x)] / c(psi)).

from math import log

import numpy as np

from config import (EULER_MASCHERONI, HEIGHT_LIMIT, MAX_SAMPLES, N_ESTIMATORS,
                    SPLIT_RESAMPLE_TRIES)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Equation 1: c(n) = 2 H(n-1) - 2 (n-1)/n   (R10)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_C_CACHE = {0: 0.0, 1: 0.0}


def c(n):
    """Average path length of an unsuccessful search in a BST of n nodes."""
    n = int(n)
    if n in _C_CACHE:
        return _C_CACHE[n]
    if n <= 1000:
        # exact harmonic number H(n-1) = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k
        h = float(np.sum(1.0 / np.arange(1, n)))
    else:
        # paper's estimate H(i) ~ ln(i) + 0.5772156649
        h = log(n - 1) + EULER_MASCHERONI
    val = 2.0 * h - 2.0 * (n - 1) / n
    _C_CACHE[n] = val
    return val


class _Node:
    """A binary node: internal if feature is not None, otherwise external."""

    __slots__ = ("feature", "threshold", "left", "right", "size")

    def __init__(self, feature, threshold, left, right, size):
        self.feature = feature
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.size = size

    @property
    def is_external(self):
        return self.feature is None


def _leaf(size):
    return _Node(None, None, None, None, size)


class IsolationTree:
    """One iTree (Algorithm 2)."""

    def __init__(self, height_limit=HEIGHT_LIMIT, random_state=None):
        self.height_limit = int(height_limit)
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(random_state)
        self.root = None
        self.n_features = None
        self.max_depth_seen = 0

    # -- training ----------------------------------------------------------
    def fit(self, X):
        X = np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
        self.n_features = X.shape[1]
        if X.shape[0] == 0:
            raise ValueError("cannot build a tree on an empty sub-sample")
        self.root = self._grow(X, 0)
        return self

    def _grow(self, X, e):

        self.max_depth_seen = max(self.max_depth_seen, e)
        n = X.shape[0]

        if e >= self.height_limit or n <= 1:
            return _leaf(n)

        hi = X.max(axis=0)

        # R5: attribute q drawn uniformly from Q
        q = int(self.rng.integers(self.n_features))

            return _leaf(n)

def _download(url, timeout=900, retries=3):
    last = None
    for _ in range(retries):
        try:
            r = requests.get(url, timeout=timeout, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
            if r.status_code == 200 and r.content:
                return r.content
            last = "HTTP %s" % r.status_code
        except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001
            last = repr(exc)
    raise RuntimeError("download failed for %s (%s)" % (url, last))


def _cached(url, fname):
    os.makedirs(DATA_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, fname)
    if os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) > 0:
        return path
    blob = _download(url)
    with open(path, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(blob)
    return path


def _zip_member(path, suffixes):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:

    url = UCI_STATIC + "52/ionosphere.zip"

"""Reproduce the Isolation Forest Table 3 AUC claims from the paper.

Run:  python reproduce.py                # smoke test + all available claims
      python reproduce.py --smoke        # smoke test only
      python reproduce.py --claims C1 C5 # selected claims
      python reproduce.py --all-datasets # also print dataset diagnostics

The paper's Table 3 trains and scores the same full data set (there is no held
out split); that protocol is reproduced as stated (assumption A6) and repeated
over several random seeds (A16).  All reported numbers are computed here.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import time

import numpy as np

import config
import data as data_mod
import evaluate
from iforest import IsolationForest, c


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_and_score(X, n_estimators, max_samples, seed):
    forest = IsolationForest(n_estimators=n_estimators, max_samples=max_samples,
                             random_state=seed)
    t0 = time.time()
    forest.fit(X)
    t_fit = time.time() - t0
    t0 = time.time()
    scores = forest.score_samples(X)
    t_score = time.time() - t0
    return forest, scores, t_fit, t_score


def tree_depths(forest):
    """Structural audit of every iTree (R1/R2/R3)."""
    max_depth = 0
    leaves = 0
    min_leaf = None
    for tree in forest.trees:
        stack = [(tree.root, 0)]
        while stack:
            node, d = stack.pop()
            max_depth = max(max_depth, d)
            if node.is_external:
                leaves += 1
                assert node.size >= 1, "external node with size < 1"
                assert node.left is None and node.right is None
                min_leaf = node.size if min_leaf is None else min(min_leaf, node.size)
            else:
                assert node.left is not None and node.right is not None, \
                    "internal node without exactly two daughters"
                assert node.left is not node.right
                assert tree.n_features is None or 0 <= node.feature < tree.n_features
                stack.append((node.left, d + 1))
                stack.append((node.right, d + 1))
    return max_depth, leaves, min_leaf


def run_claim(name, n_repeats, seed_base, verbose=True):
    spec = config.DATASETS[name]
    X, y, info = data_mod.load_dataset(name, spec)
    n, d = X.shape
    shape_ok = (n == spec["n"] and d == spec["d"])
    if spec["n_anomalies"] is not None:
        shape_ok = shape_ok and int(y.sum()) == spec["n_anomalies"]
    if verbose:
        print("  %s: X=%s anomalies=%d (%.2f%%)" % (name, X.shape, int(y.sum()),
                                                    100.0 * y.mean()))
    aucs, fits, scores_t = [], [], []
    first_audit = None
    for r in range(n_repeats):
        seed = seed_base + r
        forest, s, t_fit, t_score = build_and_score(
            X, config.N_ESTIMATORS, config.MAX_SAMPLES, seed)
        aucs.append(evaluate.auc(y, s))
        fits.append(t_fit)
        scores_t.append(t_score)
        if r == 0:
            max_depth, leaves, min_leaf = tree_depths(forest)
            paths, psi = forest.mean_path_length(X)
            first_audit = {
                "height_limit": forest.height_limit,
                "subsample_size": int(psi),
                "max_tree_depth": int(max_depth),
                "n_external_nodes": int(leaves),
                "min_external_node_size": int(min_leaf),
                "mean_path_len_normal": float(paths[y == 0].mean()),
                "mean_path_len_anomaly": float(paths[y == 1].mean()),
                "score_min": float(s.min()),
                "score_max": float(s.max()),
                "all_scores_finite": bool(np.isfinite(s).all()),
                "within_unit_interval": bool((s > 0).all() and (s <= 1).all()),
            }
        if verbose:
            print("    seed %d: AUC=%.4f (fit %.2fs, score %.2fs)"
                  % (seed, aucs[-1], t_fit, t_score))
    agg = evaluate.aggregate(aucs)
    result = {
        "claim_id": spec["claim"],
        "dataset": name,
        "n": int(n),
        "d": int(d),
        "n_anomalies": int(y.sum()),
        "anomaly_rate": float(y.mean()),
        "paper_n": spec["n"],
        "paper_d": spec["d"],
        "shape_matches_contract": bool(shape_ok),
        "auc_mean": agg["mean"],
        "auc_std": agg["std"],
        "auc_min": agg["min"],
        "auc_max": agg["max"],
        "per_seed_auc": agg["values"],
        "n_seeds": int(n_repeats),
        "runtime_sec": float(sum(fits) + sum(scores_t)),
        "fit_time_sec_per_seed": float(np.mean(fits)),
        "score_time_sec_per_seed": float(np.mean(scores_t)),
        "data_source": info["url"],
        "data_note": info["note"],
        "preprocessing": spec["preprocessing"],
        "split": "full dataset; iForest trained on sub-samples and scored on the same "
                 "rows (Table 3 protocol)",
        "audit_first_seed": first_audit,
    }
    return result


def run_smoke():
    """Download -> fit -> path length -> score -> AUC on a small slice."""
    X, y, info = data_mod.load_dataset("Ionosphere", config.DATASETS["Ionosphere"])
    sub = config.SMOKE["n_subset"]
